lines.text: the same time— warning which must lead to comfort, to
the only comfort possible; that we should take up our pain
and despair as a sharing of the cross of Christ, that we should
take it into the heart of our solitariness before God, and so
gain a part in Christ's victory over the world.
Hence to experience "that day" means: in following
Christ to take up His cross and to penetrate to that depth of
life where we are alone in God's presence, and thus to
become as one who no more belongs to this world. To such
a one the right way of prayer is granted.
What then is the right way of prayer? We need not speak
much longer on this theme, for the fact is that we have been
speaking of it essentially all the time! "If you ask anything
of the Father, He will give it to you in my name. Hitherto
you have asked nothing in my name." The right way
of prayer is prayer in the name of Christ. The disciples
had prayed much and often already before the passion and
Easter, but not 'in His name". They had prayed: "Thy
kingdom come, give us this day our daily bread" and all that
belongs to this context. They are not now to offer a different
prayer, but they are to pray differently. "In the name of
Jesus" means in the light of His cross and His victory over
the world. No doubt they are meant to pour forth to God
the sorrows and the desires of their heart, but as men who
are inwardly prepared for renunciation and sacrifice, and
who are therefore without fear or dismay. Can then the
promise that God will grant us our requests simply mean
that we can count on the fulfilment of all our wishes?
Certainly not! Yet in a deeper sense, yes. For if we pray in
His name, that is, in freedom from the bondage of self, then
in all that we ask for we are at bottom praying for encounter
with God, for the life which God bestows. To pray in the
name of Jesus means to pray as Jesus prayed in the garden
of Gethsemane, to accompany every prayer by the qualifica-
tion: "Nevertheless not my will, but Thine, be done."
